text: dsh-kicad 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 KiCad 电子设计工具集。它通过 DSH 工具、斜杠命令和右侧栏接入 KiCad，并由 Python sidecar 调用 KiCad 命令行处理设计文件。用户可以读取和编辑原理图、从原理图同步并布局 PCB、运行 ERC/DRC、执行 SPICE 或受支持 MCU 的固件仿真，并生成制造文件；侧栏还可交互查看原理图与电路板的 2D/3D 视图。适合用对话式 agent 辅助电子设计、验证和打样准备。需要本机安装 KiCad 与 Python；仿真和自动布线等功能还需要对应的外部工具。

dsh-kicad adds KiCad tools to DSH Web for editing schematics, synchronizing and routing PCBs, running ERC/DRC and circuit simulations, and exporting fabrication files. Its sidebar previews designs in interactive, SVG, and 3D views. Requires KiCad and Python.
我想让 DSH 帮我画 KiCad 原理图，并检查电气规则。
能不能从原理图同步生成 PCB，再帮我摆放元件和布线？
我需要验证电路的电压、电流或频率响应是否符合要求。
想把设计好的电路板导出成 Gerber、钻孔和 BOM 文件。
有没有工具能在侧边栏里预览原理图和 PCB 的 3D 外观？
我想检查 MCU 引脚连接，或者用提供的固件模拟板上行为。
Can an agent help me design and validate a KiCad schematic and PCB?
I want to simulate my circuit and export fabrication files from DSH.
dsh-kicad 的功能「原理图编辑」：通过工具批量创建、读取和修改 KiCad 原理图，可放置元件、连线和标签，并运行 ERC 检查结果。
dsh-kicad 的功能「PCB 同步与编辑」：从原理图更新电路板，再设置外形、摆放封装、布线、添加覆铜区和丝印，并运行 DRC。
dsh-kicad 的功能「自动布线」：调用 Freerouting 为 PCB 自动布线，可限定或排除网络；完成后检查 DRC。
dsh-kicad 的功能「电路仿真」：导出 KiCad 网表并由 ngspice 执行直流、瞬态或交流分析，按用户给出的探针和断言判断结果。
dsh-kicad 的功能「制造输出」：运行制造商设计规则检查后，可导出 Gerber、钻孔、装配位置、BOM 和可选格式，打包为订单文件。
dsh-kicad 的功能「设计文件查看器」：右侧栏识别 KiCad 原理图和 PCB，可切换交互视图、SVG 以及 PCB 的 3D 视图。
dsh-kicad 的功能「MCU 检查与模拟」：对 MCU 接线执行静态检查，并可对支持的 ATtiny 或 ESP32 固件进行板级行为模拟。

dsh-kicad README · dsh-kicad：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

KiCad for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh): a native dsh plugin bundle that lets the agent read, edit and check KiCad schematics, with KiCad itself (`kicad-cli`) deciding whether the design is correct.

> Developer preview. Built and tested against dsh `0.2.1-rc.2` and KiCad `10.0.7`. dsh's plugin APIs are pre-stable, so every package pins `engines.dsh` to `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`.

dsh-kicad README · What you get：| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Tools** (`kicad_*`) | `doctor` (is this machine ready: kicad-cli and KiCad 8+, libraries, Python, with fixes and install commands), `read_schematic`, `list_components`, `get_symbol_pins`, `list_nets` (KiCad netlist), `search_symbols` (installed libraries), `erc`, `drc`, `render` (SVG, PNG attached as an image for image-capable models; for boards KiCad's 3D view from any side or angle), `export` (netlist/BOM), `simulate` (SPICE verification with ngspice: operating point, transient and AC runs, with requirement assertions judged on the numbers, see [Simulation](#simulation)), `sim_model` (find the SPICE models in a model file or folder, with their pins), `check_mcu` (static check of how a microcontroller is wired, see [MCU wiring check](#mcu-wiring-check)), `datasheet` (read a part's datasheet PDF: its sections, search, whole pages) and `check_design` (unit tests for the schematic, quoted from the datasheets; see [Datasheet checks](#datasheet-checks)), `simulate_firmware` (run an ATtiny or ESP32 firmware against the board, see [Firmware against the board](#firmware-against-the-board)), `export_fab` (Gerber/drill

dsh-kicad README · Architecture：```
dsh-kicad-bundle  (cordis.patch.yml: global rows + presets/eda.patch.yml)
├─ dsh-kicad-bridge     Host  ctx.kicad service; runs the Python sidecar through ctx.subprocess, speaks MCP to it
│    └─ sidecar/        Python ≥3.10, stdlib-only core: lossless .kicad_sch S-expression editing, symbol libraries,
│                       pin geometry, kicad-cli (ERC/DRC/netlist/BOM/SVG), fab output; optional extras: png (cairosvg), ipc (kicad-python)

Design decisions:

dsh-kicad README · Architecture：- **Files first, headless.** Schematics are edited as files (`.kicad_sch` S-expressions) and judged with `kicad-cli`; no KiCad GUI is needed. The IPC API (`kipy`) is only an optional live channel (`ipc_status`), because it needs a running GUI and admits one client at a time.
- **Python sidecar**, not Node → IPC: KiCad's IPC is NNG + protobuf with an official binding only for Python.
- **KiCad decides.** ERC/DRC verdicts come from `kicad-cli`, never from the model.
- **Narrow dsh coupling.** Each package touches dsh only through one adapter module (`src/dsh.ts`, `src/client/dsh.ts`); the Client uses public seams only (`sidebarRightTabs`, keyed slots, `remote.workspaceFiles`, `remote.commands`, config forms) and imports no dsh Client package, as dsh asks of third-party UI plugins.

dsh-kicad README · Requirements：- dsh `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3` (`npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`), Node `>=22.19`, pnpm 11 (for building from source)
- Python `>=3.10` on `PATH` (`python3`; `python` on Windows) — no Python packages needed for the core
- KiCad 8+ with `kicad-cli` (tested with 10.0.7). Found via the setting, `$KICAD_CLI`, `PATH`, macOS/Windows install dirs, or Flatpak `org.kicad.KiCad`
- Optional: `rsvg-convert`, ImageMagick or the `png` extra for PNG renders; the `ipc` extra for the IPC channel; [ngspice](https://ngspice.sourceforge.io/) (`ngspice` on `PATH`, or `$NGSPICE`) for `kicad_simulate`; `pdftotext` from poppler (`poppler-utils`; or `$PDFTOTEXT`) for `kicad_datasheet`

dsh-kicad README · Check your setup and install KiCad：**Plugins → KiCad → KiCad bridge** shows the environment check: each item (kicad-cli, KiCad version ≥ 8, symbol and footprint libraries, Python ≥ 3.10, optional KiCad 3D models, PNG rasterizer and kicad-python) with its status and how to fix it. `/kicad-doctor` prints the same in a conversation, and the model has `kicad_doctor`; a tool that fails because KiCad is missing names the install command.

dsh-kicad README · From source (works today)：```sh
git clone https://github.com/LuYanFCP/dsh-kicad && cd dsh-kicad
pnpm install && pnpm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/packages/kicad-bundle"
dsh web

`dsh plugin … add <dir>` links the directory; leaf packages resolve through this checkout's `node_modules`, and dsh maps `@deepseek-ai/*` imports to the running installation. Rebuild and restart dsh after code changes. In the Web UI you can also use **Plugins → Install** with the same absolute path.

dsh-kicad README · Paste the repository URL (simplest)：In dsh, **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter `https://github.com/LuYanFCP/dsh-kicad` and install (or `dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/LuYanFCP/dsh-kicad`). The repository root is itself the `dsh-kicad` bundle; it loads the prebuilt `dist/dsh-kicad`. Append `#<tag-or-commit>` to pin a version.

dsh-kicad README · From the plugin market (search inside dsh)：dsh finds plugins through **plugin markets**: JSON indexes you add once. This repository publishes one.

1. **Plugins → Experimental plugins → More → Custom plugin markets**: switch it on. A **Discover** tab appears.
2. **Discover → Add index source**: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LuYanFCP/dsh-kicad/main/market/index.json`
3. Search, e.g. `kicad`, `原理图`, `电路板`, `circuit board`, then **Install → Enable now**. No restart needed.

text:
dsh-kicad README · Use：1. Open a session whose workspace contains a KiCad project (sidebar **Add workspace**). Optionally pick the **EDA agent** preset.
2. Ask, e.g. *"Add a 100 nF decoupling capacitor between +3V3 and GND next to U1 and make ERC pass."* The agent reads the design, sends one `kicad_edit_schematic` batch (you approve it), and reads the ERC verdict that the policy appends.
3. Open the `.kicad_sch` from **Workspace files**: the KiCad tab shows the render, refreshed after each agent edit; **Render** re-renders on demand.
4. `/erc`, `/drc`, `/bom` work without the model.
5. **Plugins → KiCad → KiCad bridge / KiCad policy** hold the settings.

dsh-kicad README · Schematics by functional block：A new design is drawn block by block, like a reference design. The agent first plans the blocks (title, parts, area on the page). It then builds one block per `kicad_edit_schematic` call and frames it with `add_block`: a dashed frame titled with the block's job and main part (`3V3 LDO — AMS1117-3.3`, `MCU — ATtiny85`), with short notes inside where a choice needs explaining. Blocks connect only through net labels and power symbols. After every batch that places or moves parts, the edit result names the parts outside every block, and the agent is not done while there are any. `kicad_read_schematic` lists the same parts as `outside_blocks`. An existing schematic keeps its organisation unless you ask to reorganise it. The board placement below follows the same blocks.

dsh-kicad README · Datasheet checks：A part's limits and the parts it needs come from its datasheet, not from the model's memory. `kicad_datasheet {path, reference | lib_id | url | pdf, query?, pages?}` reads the datasheet: the symbol's own link, a URL the agent found with `web_search`, or a PDF in the workspace. It downloads the PDF once into `.dsh-kicad/datasheets/`, extracts the text per page with `pdftotext`, and returns the pages of the usual sections (absolute maximum ratings, operating conditions, electrical characteristics, application information, layout), the lines matching a query, or whole pages. A link that leads to a web page or a zip is refused with what to do instead.

dsh-kicad README · Datasheet checks：`kicad_check_design` turns those pages into unit tests for the schematic. Each check states one requirement and quotes the words it comes from. The checks are kept in `design-checks.json` next to the schematic, and the tool judges them on KiCad's netlist and the part values. Rules:

dsh-kicad README · Datasheet checks：A check counts only when its source holds: the quote must be in the datasheet text (or in a workspace file such as `design-brief.md`, for the user's own numbers), and it must state the check's numbers. Otherwise the check is CANNOT VERIFY, never passed. After every schematic edit the checks re-run and the failing ones are appended to the result; `/design-checks` runs them without the model.

dsh-kicad README · Datasheet checks：On the AMS1117-3.3 the datasheet says "The addition of 22µF solid tantalum on the output will ensure stability for all operating conditions". A design with the usual 10 µF fails that check (`capacitance +3V3 → GND = 10.1 µF < 22 µF`); with 22 µF it passes. The `kicad-datasheet-checks` skill says what to take from each kind of part.

dsh-kicad README · Board placement：After `kicad_update_pcb` creates a board, one `kicad_edit_pcb` operation, `auto_place`, lays it out from the schematic's functional blocks (the `add_block` frames; without them its sheets, else net connectivity): each block stays together, connectors sit on the board edge facing out (a footprint's "PCB Edge" mark lands on the edge), decoupling capacitors go next to their IC's power pins and crystals next to their IC, power parts get extra room, and the outline is sized to fit (a drawn outline is kept and filled instead). `place_block` lays out one block in a given spot or rectangle. `kicad_read_pcb` then reports courtyard overlaps, footprints outside the outline and the total ratsnest length, and `kicad_render` with `view: "3d"` shows the result. On the usb-attiny85 board it gives no courtyard overlap, everything inside the outline, the USB-C on the edge, and a ratsnest of 214 mm against 345 mm for random placement ([details](docs/pcb-architecture.md#placement-12)).

dsh-kicad README · Routing：`kicad_autoroute {pcb, nets?, exclude_nets?, passes?, timeout?}` writes the board as a Specctra design, runs Freerouting headless, and adds only the new tracks and vias; footprints never move. Every track and via already on the board is fixed wiring, so the agent routes critical nets by hand first (power, USB or differential pairs, a crystal: `kicad_edit_pcb` `add_track` / `add_via` with `locked: true`) and the router completes the rest. Copper zones (a GND pour on both layers) are refilled and saved afterwards by `kicad-cli pcb drc --refill-zones --save-board`, whose verdict (unrouted count, DRC errors, schematic parity) is the result. The run can be cancelled from dsh and stops at `timeout` (default 300 s), keeping what it routed; the design, session and log stay in `<project>/.dsh-kicad/autoroute/`. When connections stay open, the result suggests routing them by hand or, on an `auto_place`d board, clearing the routes (`remove_tracks`) and placing again with more room (`gap: 2, group_gap: 4`): that routes the usb-attiny85 example completely.

dsh-kicad README · Routing：Freerouting (GPL-3.0) is a separate Java program and is not bundled. `/kicad-doctor` checks for Java and Freerouting; `/kicad-install freerouting --yes` downloads the pinned release jar (2.5.0, about 65 MB, SHA-256 checked) into your data directory (`~/.local/share/dsh-kicad/freerouting` on Linux), never with `sudo`. Freerouting 2.5.0 needs **Java 25+**: the doctor lists the package-manager command or the [Temurin JRE](https://adoptium.net/temurin/releases/?package=jre). The bridge's `java` and `freerouting` settings point at an existing Java or jar.

dsh-kicad README · Simulation：`kicad_simulate {path, analyses?, assertions?, probes?, timeout?}` checks what a schematic *does*, not only how it is wired. KiCad exports the SPICE netlist (`kicad-cli sch export netlist --format spice`, which reads the symbols' `Sim.*` properties, so a design simulated here also simulates in KiCad's own Simulator), ngspice runs it headless, and each requirement is an assertion the tool judges on the numbers, as ERC and DRC are judged by KiCad: the model never decides.

dsh-kicad README · Simulation：- Analyses: `op` (DC operating point, the default), `tran {stop, step?}`, `ac {start, stop, points?}`; one of each per call.
- Probes: `V(net)`, `V(a,b)`, `I(R1|C1|L1|D1|V1)`. Assertions: `{probe, min?, max?, equals? + tol | tol_pct, abs?, measure?, at?, from?, to?, ref?}` with SPICE-style numbers (`10k`, `100n`, `3.3`, `20m`). Measures: `final`, `initial`, `max`, `min`, `mean`, `rms`, `pp`, `at` (transient); `gain_db`, `phase_deg`, `peak_gain_db`, `lowpass_cutoff_hz`, `highpass_cutoff_hz` (AC, `ref` for gain relative to the input).
- Example: a 3.3 V rail `{probe: "V(3V3)", min: 3.2, max: 3.4}`, an LED `{probe: "I(D1)", min: "5m", max: "15m", abs: true}`, a low-pass `{probe: "V(OUT)", analysis: "ac", measure: "lowpass_cutoff_hz", equals: 1000, tol_pct: 5}`.
- The circuit needs a ground net, sources from `Simulation_SPICE` (`VDC`, `VSIN`, `VPULSE`, `IDC`) and a model for every part that matters: R, C and L simulate from their value; a diode or LED needs `set_sim_model {reference, device: "D", params}` (hidden `Sim.Device`) (the tool refuses otherwise, because without it KiCad wires the diode backwards); ICs, regulators and transistors need a vendor mod

dsh-kicad README · MCU wiring check：`kicad_check_mcu {path, reference?, requirements?}` checks how each microcontroller is wired, from KiCad's netlist and a per-family pin table (an MCU *provider*), and judges the result itself. It is a static check, not a firmware simulation: it cannot know what the firmware does with a pin.

dsh-kicad README · MCU wiring check：- **Findings** (error / warning / info, each with the pin, the net and a fix). For the classic ESP32: a strapping pin held at the wrong level at reset (GPIO0 tied to ground, GPIO12 high or strongly pulled up, which selects 1.8 V flash and stops the chip booting, GPIO2 pulled up), reserved flash or PSRAM pins in use (GPIO6-11, and 16/17 on PICO, WROVER and the -R2 modules), an input-only GPIO (34-39) that nothing can drive or that floats behind a button, an unconnected or unpulled EN, less than 10 µF on the supply. For the ATtiny85: RESET unconnected or relying on the weak internal pull-up, less than 100 nF on VCC; its peripherals sit on fixed pins, so requirements like `i2c_sda`, `i2c_scl`, `spi_*`, `pwm`, `adc` are judged against them (an I²C SDA on PB4 fails). For the ATmega48/88/168/328 (the Arduino UNO/Nano chip; pins named by port, PB0-PD7): RESET unpulled, VCC and AVCC decoupling, AVCC that does not reach VCC (the datasheet wants it connected even without the ADC; an LC filter counts), AREF tied straight to a rail (selecting the AVCC or 1.1 V reference would short it) or without its capacitor, a crystal on XTAL1/XTAL2 without load capacitor

dsh-kicad README · Firmware against the board：`kicad_simulate_firmware {path, firmware?, stimuli?, assertions?, duration?, clock_hz?, ...}` runs a firmware image on a simulated **ATtiny25/45/85** or **classic ESP32** wired as the schematic says and judges what the board does, so "pressing the button lights the LED within 20 ms" is checked rather than assumed. The firmware is one you built: for the ATtiny a `.hex` or `.elf` (avr-gcc, PlatformIO, Arduino; an ELF also carries the initial EEPROM), for the ESP32 a merged flash image (see below); the plugin never builds, writes or invents one.

dsh-kicad README · Firmware against the board：- **The chip** is a pure-Python AVR simulator (no dependencies) that follows the datasheet (Atmel 2586Q, read in full for this): the ATtiny25/45/85 instruction set and memory sizes; GPIO; the external, pin-change and every peripheral interrupt in vector order; **Timer0 and Timer1** (normal, CTC, phase-correct and fast PWM, toggle outputs; compare values latched at TOP/BOTTOM as the hardware does; Timer1 with the 64 MHz PLL clock, OCR1C as TOP and the complementary outputs); the **ADC** (single-ended and differential channels with gain, unipolar and bipolar, the bandgap, the temperature sensor, Vcc / 1.1 V / 2.56 V / AREF references, free running, the 13/25-clock conversion time); the **analog comparator**; **EEPROM** (3.4 ms writes, erase-only and write-only modes, persisting across resets, loaded from an ELF's `.eeprom`); the **watchdog** (reset and interrupt mode, the timed-sequence rules, wake-up from power-down); **resets** (the RESET pin, the watchdog, the 64 ms start-up delay, MCUSR flags); the **USI in three-wire mode** (SPI as master or slave, software strobe or external clock); idle and power-down sleep. It is checked against p

dsh-kicad README · Firmware against the board：**The classic ESP32** (WROOM/WROVER modules and PICO) runs on [Espressif's QEMU](https://github.com/espressif/qemu) (`qemu-system-xtensa -machine esp32`): the ROM, the second-stage bootloader, your application and FreeRTOS on both cores, so an ESP-IDF or Arduino-ESP32 build runs as it is. QEMU is a separate install: `kicad_doctor` reports it, `/kicad-install qemu-esp32` downloads Espressif's release (checked against its SHA-256, no root), and the one ESP-IDF installs (`idf_tools.py install qemu-xtensa`) is found too; the `qemu` setting or `$QEMU_XTENSA` points to another.

dsh-kicad README · Firmware against the board：- **Firmware**: the merged flash image (bootloader at 0x1000, partition table, application: ESP-IDF's `esptool.py --chip esp32 merge_bin -o flash.bin @flash_args` in the build folder, or Arduino's `.merged.bin`), or the build folder's `flasher_args.json`, which is merged for you. It is padded to a flash size QEMU accepts; the file itself is never written.
- **The pins.** QEMU's ESP32 GPIO peripheral is a stub and IO_MUX and RTC_IO are not modelled, so the sidecar watches the chip through QEMU's gdb stub and does every load and store of those registers itself: outputs, open drain, the internal pull-ups and pull-downs, input enables and the GPIO matrix follow the firmware, a read-modify-write (ESP-IDF's way of setting a pad up) starts from what the chip holds, and a load of `GPIO_IN` gets the levels the board gives the pins. Pins are `GPIO2`, `IO2` or `U1:IO2` in assertions. The board side is the same DC network (pin drivers by drive strength, about 33 Ω at the default; 45 kΩ pulls; ESP32 thresholds).
- **Boot and reset.** The strapping pins (GPIO0, 2, 4, 5, 12, 15) are solved at power-on and handed to QEMU: holding GPIO0 low really start

dsh-kicad README · 3D view：Open a `.kicad_pcb` and pick **3D** next to Interactive / SVG, much like KiCad's View → 3D Viewer. The Host exports the board as a binary glTF scene (`kicad-cli pcb export glb` with copper, pads, zones, mask, silkscreen and the footprints' 3D models) into `<project>/.dsh-kicad/render/<board>/`, cached by board content, so reopening is instant. The view reads it through `remote.workspaceFiles` (raw bytes; 2 MiB windows beyond dsh's 32 MiB whole-file limit) and shows it with three.js: drag to rotate, right- or Shift-drag to pan, scroll to zoom; **Top / Bottom / Front / Back / Left / Right / Iso**, **Perspective / Orthographic**, **Components** and **Reset view**. When the board changes (an agent edit, KiCad saving) it is exported again after a quiet second and the camera stays where it was; a failed export keeps the last good model and says why.

dsh-kicad README · 3D view：**KiCad render** renders the current camera with KiCad's own renderer (`kicad-cli pcb render --quality high`, a few seconds), mapping the orbit camera to `--rotate` / `--zoom` / `--pivot` / `--perspective`, for KiCad's exact look. Without WebGL the 3D mode shows such renders, with the same view buttons.

three.js (about 645 KB, 163 KB gzipped) is a separate client chunk, `lib/client.three.js`, that dsh loads the first time a board opens in 3D; the main client module grew by about 28 KB.

dsh-kicad README · Fab output：`/kicad-fab [board.kicad_pcb] [--preset jlcpcb|pcbway] [--force] [--step] [--ipc2581] [--odb]` (the agent's `kicad_export_fab`) lets KiCad judge the board first. DRC errors, unrouted connections, schematic parity issues (when the schematic sits next to the board) and, with a preset, errors against that fab's limits refuse the export, and nothing is written. `--force` exports anyway; the result and `fab-manifest.json` say so.

dsh-kicad README · Fab output：Output goes to `<project>/fab/<preset or kicad>/`: Gerbers for copper, mask, paste, silkscreen and Edge.Cuts with the Gerber job file; Excellon drill files with a Gerber X2 drill map; `assembly/` with the position CSV and BOM (plus JLC BOM/CPL with `--preset jlcpcb`); `preview/` with front and back 3D PNGs; and `<board>-<preset or fab>.zip` with everything except the previews.

dsh-kicad README · Fab output：`kicad_fab_preset` makes a fab's limits (minimum track, clearance, drill, annular ring, hole spacing, copper to edge) the project's design rules, so `kicad_drc` checks what the fab can make: board setup minimums go into the `.kicad_pro`, custom rules into a managed block of the `.kicad_dru` (your own rules stay). The values come from each fab's published capabilities ([`presets/`](packages/kicad-bridge/sidecar/src/dsh_kicad_sidecar/presets)); the fab's own review has the last word.

dsh-kicad README · Known limitations：- Boards are created and kept in sync from the schematic (`kicad_update_pcb`), placed (`auto_place`), edited, routed (`kicad_autoroute`), checked and exported (`kicad_export_fab`). Autorouting needs Java 25+ and Freerouting, which are installed separately (see [Routing](#routing)); dense boards may keep a few unrouted connections for the agent to finish by hand.
- Simulation covers analog behaviour with ngspice; parts without a SPICE model are left out, and firmware, signal integrity, EMC and thermal behaviour are not simulated. Plain Device:LED / Device:D symbols need `Sim.Device` set (see [Simulation](#simulation)).
- Firmware simulation covers the ATtiny25/45/85 and the classic ESP32 (on Espressif's QEMU, a separate install); it refuses what it does not model (see [Firmware against the board](#firmware-against-the-board); on the ESP32 among others deep sleep, pads driven by I2C, SPI or RMT, WiFi and Bluetooth). MCU checks are otherwise static and only cover families with a provider (classic ESP32, the 8-pin ATtiny25/45/85, the ATmega48/88/168/328 and the Arduino Nano/UNO today; the ATmega328P's firmware simulation is in progress); other MCUs
